A COLLECTION OF LEGAL ROLE-PLAYING GAMES

The Legal RPG Library

Eine triviale Komödie für ernsthafte Leute — with apologies to Oscar Wilde.

Ten small browser games about the legal profession, played with twenty-sided dice: the hearing room, the expert’s chair, the war room, the arbitral tribunal, the law firm, and the journeys in between.

Pick a role, watch the dice, keep your coffee bar filled. No account, no install, no mercy from the printer.

The dice do not bill by the hour.

How to play

Each book opens a standalone browser game. Choose your role, make decisions and roll a twenty-sided die (D20). Your choices, professional strengths and the dice determine how the week unfolds. Watch your resources: professional reputation, stamina, coffee and the occasional deadline.

The games are self-contained HTML files. They run in a modern browser, without an account or installation. For offline play, keep this index and the game files together in one folder.

Colophon

These games were built in long conversation with Claude, Anthropic's AI assistant — co-author, tireless playtester, and patient re-collator of bundles. Which gives the library a second, quieter joke: it is also a portrait of what an AI, raised on the profession's collective writing, imagines the law to feel like — the hearing weeks and the partners' retreats, the billable targets and the pink message slips, the journeys between meetings and airports; the war stories, the understatement, the reverence for the record, the pastries. A portrait, though, is not a photograph: the model learned the profession from what the internet chose to write down, and the internet records its grievances far more diligently than its ordinary Tuesdays. Some hardships in these games are therefore exaggerated, others are satire outright, and the all-nighters arrive at a frequency no real firm would recognise, let alone accept. None of it should be confused with reality — least of all with any actual firm, colleague, case or client. If practitioners recognise themselves in these rooms anyway, the credit belongs to everyone who ever wrote the war stories down. The judgment calls, the professional realism and the final say remained, throughout, human. This is a loving tribute to tabletop games of my past, and I assert no rights into any of the concepts or ideas used. If you have any issues, contact me under richard.happ@me.com.
